edges.limitations: Species, non-native promoter, unestablished physiological mutant-to-wild-type ratio and allele specificity limit transfer to human DFNA3A. The clinical spectrum is not uniformly congenital or profound; auditory absence at every possible age is not established.

nodes.description: Preclinical adenine base editing of p.Arg75Trp restored neurobiotin transfer in an engineered HeLa model and improved gap-junction plaque morphology in mouse cochlear supporting cells. The study used P0 cochlear explants and intracochlear delivery to adult transgenic mice aged 9–30 weeks, with morphology assessed two weeks later. In HeLa cells, 46.8% on-target editing included bystander changes; 28.03% reads were corrected without bystanders. Adult plaque improvement does not establish auditory rescue: baseline ABR characterized the model, but no post-treatment hearing-rescue result was reported. Functional treatment windows, durability, delivery and editing safety remain unresolved.

nodes.description: Human p.Arg75Trp transgenic mice show supporting-cell deformation, absent tunnel of Corti and Nuel space, reduced inner-pillar-cell microtubules and severe-to-profound hearing loss. The original report established two independent transgenic lines; later studies extend this allele/model system rather than establish the lesion in human DFNA3A. Sensory-cell development was preserved at P5–P12, and isolated outer hair cells retained nonlinear capacitance despite absent otoacoustic emissions. This supports a contribution from the supporting-cell environment, without proving that every dominant human allele causes the same developmental defect.

nodes.description: p.Trp44Cys co-expressed with wild-type connexin 26 at an equal ratio in Xenopus oocytes strongly reduces intercellular conductance and alters residual gating. The recessive p.Trp77Arg comparator does not inhibit wild-type channel formation or gating in the same assay. p.Arg75Trp forms hemichannels with altered voltage dependence and reduced permeability but fails to form functional intercellular channels; its dominant effect is at the gap-junction channel level. These results establish functional interference, not degradation of wild-type protein or exclusive proof of a docking defect. Dominant inheritance and clinical scope still require human evidence; an in-vitro inhibition assay alone is insufficient.

nodes.description: Reduced gap-junction communication in cochlear supporting cells is a proposed tissue consequence of allele-specific connexin 26 dysfunction. Human cochlear expression supplies anatomical context, while dominant inhibition is measured mainly in heterologous cells. A separate Gjb6/Cx30 T5M homozygous knock-in model had approximately 15-dB hearing loss, normal electrical coupling in developing cochlea and reduced calcein transfer and calcium signaling. Connexin 26 and 30 abundance was also reduced, so that model does not isolate biochemical coupling as the sole cause or directly establish the DFNA3A mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: The human deafness-associated connexin 30 T5M mutation causes mild hearing loss and reduces biochemical coupling among cochlear non-sensory cells in knock-in mice.
evidence.snippet: In the developing cochlea, electrical coupling, probed by dual patch-clamp recordings, was normal. However, transfer of the fluorescent tracer calcein between cochlear non-sensory cells was reduced, as was intercellular Ca(2+) signalling due to spontaneous ATP release from connexin hemichannels.

nodes.description: Impaired supporting-cell potassium handling could disturb the extracellular cortilymph surrounding hair cells. This was proposed from p.Arg75Trp mouse findings, not measured directly. Normal endolymphatic resting potential and preserved strial structure constrain an endocochlear-potential-loss account but neither measure cortilymph potassium nor establish that every aspect of endolymph homeostasis is normal.

Endolymphatic resting potential was preserved, but cortilymph potassium was not directly measured.
